name: Vincristine
route_note: IV only, usually as a short infusion in a minibag; fatal if given intrathecally

discovery.by: Gordon Svoboda and colleagues, Eli Lilly
discovery.note: Isolated from the Madagascar periwinkle (Catharanthus roseus) after Noble and Beer at the University of Western Ontario discovered vinblastine in 1958.

tagline: Periwinkle alkaloid central to childhood leukaemia and lymphoma treatment
summary: Vincristine is a vinca alkaloid that binds tubulin and prevents microtubule assembly, arresting dividing cells in metaphase. It is a key component of treatment for acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, lymphomas and paediatric solid tumours; its dose-limiting toxicity is peripheral neuropathy rather than marrow suppression.
mechanism: Vincristine binds the vinca domain at the β-tubulin plus end, inhibiting polymerisation and promoting microtubule disassembly at higher concentrations.

Without a functional mitotic spindle, chromosomes cannot segregate and cells arrest in metaphase and die. Disruption of axonal microtubule transport causes the characteristic sensory-motor and autonomic neuropathy.
uses: Wilms tumour, neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma
Small-cell lung cancer and brain tumours in some regimens

history.title: Vinblastine
history.detail: Robert Noble and Charles Beer isolate vinblastine while investigating periwinkle as a folk diabetes remedy.

history.title: Vincristine isolated
history.detail: Lilly scientists isolate leurocristine (vincristine) from periwinkle.

history.title: POMP and VAMP
history.detail: Combination regimens containing vincristine help drive childhood ALL cure rates upward.

history.title: Liposomal vincristine
history.detail: Marqibo approved for relapsed Philadelphia-negative ALL (later withdrawn in 2022).

history.title: Supply shortage
history.detail: A US shortage after a manufacturer exit raises concern for paediatric oncology.

serious: severe neurotoxicity with CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. azoles)
fatal ascending paralysis if given intrathecally
safety.boxed_warning: Boxed warning: for IV use only — fatal if given by other routes; extravasation causes severe tissue injury.

facts: About 500 kg of periwinkle leaves yield roughly 1 g of vincristine.
Inadvertent intrathecal injection has caused dozens of deaths, prompting the dispensing of vincristine in minibags instead of syringes.
